purpose: Evaluation-only hierarchical taxonomy used to decide exact / one-level-broader / unrelated / invalid comparisons. Never used by production.

sources.role: authoritative production category canonicalization; supplies level-1 values and the level-2 synonym sets
prompt-routing category set and keyword groups
Build 2 Closet taxonomy FIELD list (category, clothingType, subtype, brand, primaryColor, secondaryColors, material, size). Supplies field names only — it defines no value vocabulary.

importedCategories._comment: Level-1 values that normalizeCategory can actually RETURN. A prediction is scored against these.

routeOnlyCategories._comment: Present in scannerCategoryRoute VALID_TAXONOMY_CATEGORIES but NOT canonicalized by normalizeCategory — normalizeCategory falls through and returns the lowercased input verbatim. Recorded as a real divergence between two production sources, not silently merged.
routeOnlyCategories.rationale: The routing layer treats these as first-class apparel categories and normalizeCategory passes them through unchanged, so a prediction of 'skirt' is a stable level-1 value in practice. Scoring them as invalid would penalize the model for a divergence between two production modules.

evaluationOnlyAliases._comment: The Phase 0A seed manifest labels categories in a PLURAL vocabulary that production never emits. Scoring those labels directly against production output would mark every category wrong and report a false 0% category accuracy. These aliases are evaluation-only and resolve label vocabulary to production canonical form. They are NOT production behavior and are NOT written back to any production module.
evaluationOnlyAliases.aliasIsNotAMatch: Applying an alias yields exact_match only when the resolved values are equal. An alias never upgrades an unrelated value into a match.

disputedRelationships.productionBehavior: normalizeCategory tests blazer BEFORE outerwear and returns 'blazer', making them SIBLING level-1 categories, not parent/child.
disputedRelationships.evaluationRule: Scored as unrelated, NOT one_level_broader. Predicting 'outerwear' for a labeled 'blazer' is a category miss under production's own vocabulary.
disputedRelationships.rationale: Common fashion usage treats a blazer as outerwear. Production does not. Silently allowing the broader credit would inflate category accuracy against production's actual contract.

disputedRelationships.productionBehavior: normalizeCategory does NOT include skirt in the pants regex; 'skirt' falls through and is returned verbatim. The Phase 0A seed manifest nevertheless labels skirt cases as category 'bottoms'.
disputedRelationships.evaluationRule: skirt is treated as its own level-1 category. The eval alias bottoms->pants does NOT capture skirt. A skirt case labeled 'bottoms' is flagged invalid_comparison rather than scored.

disputedRelationships.productionBehavior: normalizeCategory places 'cardigans?' in the TOP regex, so production canonicalizes a cardigan to 'top'.
disputedRelationships.evaluationRule: cardigan is a subtype of sweater under top. Predicting 'outerwear' is unrelated.

disputedRelationships.productionBehavior: Production has no eyewear or jewelry level-1 category; both canonicalize to 'accessory'.
disputedRelationships.evaluationRule: The Phase 0B dataset plan names eyewear and jewelry as primary content targets. They are scored as clothingTypes under accessory. Reporting them as level-1 categories would imply a production capability that does not exist.

unsupportedRelationships.reason: CLOSET_ITEM_TAXONOMY_FIELDS includes 'size', but the V2 scanner result contract has no size field. Not evaluable.

resolutionLevel hierarchy exists in the contract vocabulary but normalizeToV2 passes exactProduct: null into deriveResolutionLevel, so exact_product and model_family are unreachable on the deployed scanner path. Recorded as measurement ceiling MC-1; not scored as a taxonomy relationship.
No production field. Not labeled, not scored.
